statements.subject: server
statements.description: In order to make FTP workable without needless error messages, the following minimum implementation is required for all servers:

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: All hosts must accept the above as the standard defaults.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server protocol interpreter shall "listen" on Port L.
actions: Listen on Port L for incoming control connections

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The user or user protocol interpreter shall initiate the full-duplex control connection.
actions: Initiate full-duplex control connection to server

statements.subject: participant
statements.description: Server- and user- processes should follow the conventions of the Telnet protocol as specified in the ARPA-Internet Protocol Handbook [1].

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Servers are under no obligation to provide for editing of command lines and may require that it be done in the user host.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The control connection shall be closed by the server at the user's request after all transfers and replies are completed.
actions: Close control connection

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The user-DTP must "listen" on the specified data port; this may be the default user port (U) or a port specified in the PORT command.
actions: Listen on specified data port (default port U or PORT-command-specified port)

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server shall initiate the data connection from his own default data port (L-1) using the specified user data port.
actions: Initiate data connection from port L-1 to specified user data port

statements.subject: ftp
statements.description: Note that all FTP implementation must support data transfer using the default port, and that only the USER-PI may initiate the use of non-default ports.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The user-PI may then send the corresponding service commands to A and B.
actions: Send service command to Server A
Send service command to Server B

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The data connection shall be closed by the server under the conditions described in the Section on Establishing Data Connections.
actions: Close data connection

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the data connection is to be closed following a data transfer where closing the connection is not required to indicate the end-of-file, the server must do so immediately.
actions: Close data connection immediately after transfer completes

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Waiting until after a new transfer command is not permitted because the user-process will have already tested the data connection to see if it needs to do a "listen"; (remember that the user must "listen" on a closed data port BEFORE sending the transfer request).
actions: Listen on closed data port before issuing transfer request

statements.subject: client
statements.description: To prevent a race condition here, the server sends a reply (226) after closing the data connection (or if the connection is left open, a "file transfer completed" reply (250) and the user-PI should wait for one of these replies before issuing a new transfer command).
actions: Wait for reply 226 or 250 before issuing new transfer command

statements.subject: participant
statements.description: Any time either the user or server see that the connection is being closed by the other side, it should promptly read any remaining data queued on the connection and issue the close on its own side.
actions: Read remaining data queued on connection
Issue close on own side

statements.subject: server
statements.description: It should be noted that the server is to take no action until the end of line code is received.
actions: Take no action on received command data until end-of-line code is received

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The user should wait for this initial primary success or failure response before sending further commands.
actions: Wait for primary success or failure response before sending further commands

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Certain commands require a second reply for which the user should also wait.
actions: Wait for second reply when command requires one

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The user should wait for this greeting message before sending any commands.
actions: Wait for 220 greeting message before sending any commands

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the server is unable to accept input right away, a 120 "expected delay" reply should be sent immediately and a 220 reply when ready.
actions: Send 120 reply immediately
Send 220 reply when server is ready to accept input

statements.subject: server
statements.description: It is recommended that such information be queued in the server-PI and delivered to the user-PI in the next reply (possibly making it a multi-line reply).

statements.subject: server
statements.description: These must be strictly adhered to; a server may substitute text in the replies, but the meaning and action implied by the code numbers and by the specific command reply sequence cannot be altered.
actions: Strictly adhere to command-reply sequences
Do not alter meaning implied by reply code numbers or command-reply sequence
